1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Integration: run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog (#1944)
3	#
4	# SPEC-1 [code]: a run whose wall-clock time exceeds max_run_s ends with
5	#   pipeline status timed_out in pipeline-state.json and pipeline.end event
6	#   carrying status=timed_out, the in-flight stage, and limit_s; the watchdog
7	#   fires even when the engine is idle between dispatches (not only inside a
8	#   stage); a process that ignores TERM is dead within TERM + 10 s; release and
9	#   persist execute on every timed-out exit path.
10	#
11	# Phases:
12	#   P1 — basic timeout: slow stage hits the watchdog; status=timed_out, event
13	#        fields correct; runner exits non-zero within the limit
14	#   P2 — idle between dispatches: fast-one completes before watchdog fires;
15	#        watchdog fires while fast-two is sleeping; fast-one being in "complete"
16	#        state proves the watchdog runs independently of stage dispatch state
17	#   P3 — TERM-ignore: a stage that traps and ignores SIGTERM is dead within
18	#        TERM + 10 s (KILL escalation)
19	#   P4 — release and persist run: always_run release + persist stages execute
20	#        on every timed-out exit path
21	set -uo pipefail
22	
23	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
24	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
25	RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
26	
27	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
28	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
29	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
30	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
31	
32	print_test_header "run-timed-out: wall-clock limit watchdog fires and ends run correctly (#1944)"
33	setup_test_env "run-timed-out"
34	export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
35	
36	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
37	STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
38	EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
39	EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
40	export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
41	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$EVENTS_DIR"
42	export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_JSONL"
43	export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
44	export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
45	export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
46	export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
47	mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
48	printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"
49	
50	# ── Shared overlay repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo run-timed-out-overlay)"
52	mkdir -p "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates"
53	
54	# Single-stage template: one slow stage (the main timeout victim)
55	cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
56	id: timeout-single
57	extends: simple
58	stages:
59	  - id: slow-stage
60	    gate: auto
61	    io:
62	      destinations: [file]
63	      tail_lines: 50
64	    router:
65	      timeout_s: 120
66	      max_turns: 0
67	EOF
68	
69	# Two-stage template: fast-one is instant; fast-two blocks for a long time
70	cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-two-stage.yaml" <<'EOF'
71	id: timeout-two-stage
72	extends: simple
73	stages:
74	  - id: fast-one
75	    gate: auto
76	    io:
77	      destinations: [file]
78	      tail_lines: 50
79	  - id: fast-two
80	    gate: auto
81	    io:
82	      destinations: [file]
83	      tail_lines: 50
84	EOF
85	
86	# Always-run (release + persist) template: flow stage + always_run release + persist
87	cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-with-release.yaml" <<'EOF'
88	id: timeout-with-release
89	extends: simple
90	flow:
91	  - outcome
92	
93	always_run:
94	  - release
95	  - persist-stage
96	
97	outcome:
98	  gate: auto
99	  io:
100	    destinations: [file]
101	    tail_lines: 50
102	
103	release:
104	  gate: auto
105	  roles: [teardown]
106	  router:
107	    timeout_s: 30
108	  io:
109	    destinations: [file]
110	    tail_lines: 50
111	
112	persist-stage:
113	  gate: auto
114	  roles: [persist]
115	  router:
116	    timeout_s: 30
117	  io:
118	    destinations: [file]
119	    tail_lines: 50
120	EOF
121	
122	# Commit the templates into the overlay repo so the runner can find them
123	(cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add timeout test templates") >/dev/null 2>&1
124	
125	# ── P1: basic timeout — slow stage, status=timed_out ───────────────────────
126	
127	# Stage that sleeps far longer than max_run_s
128	mock_plugin_factory "slow-stage" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
129	SLOW_STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/slow-stage-started"
130	cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG

132	    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"

134	    $(mock_result_line slow-stage)
135	    return 0
136	}

146	    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p1" ) \

156	if [[ ! -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
157	    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
158	else
159	    _p1_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
160	    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p1_status"
161	fi
162	
163	print_test_section "P1: pipeline.end event fields — status=timed_out, stage, limit_s"
164	
165	if [[ ! -f "$EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
166	    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: events.jsonl written" "events file not found"
167	else
168	    # Event: pipeline.end with status=timed_out
169	    _p1_end_event="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out")' \
170	        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
171	    if [[ -n "$_p1_end_event" ]]; then
172	        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted"
173	    else
174	        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted" \
175	            "no such event in $(wc -l < "$EVENTS_JSONL") events"
176	    fi
177	
178	    # The event must carry the in-flight stage name
179	    _p1_stage="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.stage // empty' \
180	        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
181	    if [[ -n "$_p1_stage" ]]; then
182	        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage (stage=$_p1_stage)"
183	    else

189	    _p1_limit="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.limit_s // empty' \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog (#1944)
#
# SPEC-1 [code]: a run whose wall-clock time exceeds max_run_s ends with
#   pipeline status timed_out in pipeline-state.json and pipeline.end event
#   carrying status=timed_out, the in-flight stage, and limit_s; the watchdog
#   fires even when the engine is idle between dispatches (not only inside a
#   stage); a process that ignores TERM is dead within TERM + 10 s; release and
#   persist execute on every timed-out exit path.
#
# Phases:
#   P1 — basic timeout: slow stage hits the watchdog; status=timed_out, event
#        fields correct; runner exits non-zero within the limit
#   P2 — idle between dispatches: fast-one completes before watchdog fires;
#        watchdog fires while fast-two is sleeping; fast-one being in "complete"
#        state proves the watchdog runs independently of stage dispatch state
#   P3 — TERM-ignore: a stage that traps and ignores SIGTERM is dead within
#        TERM + 10 s (KILL escalation)
#   P4 — release and persist run: always_run release + persist stages execute
#        on every timed-out exit path
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-timed-out: wall-clock limit watchdog fires and ends run correctly (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-timed-out"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_JSONL"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# ── Shared overlay repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo run-timed-out-overlay)"
mkdir -p "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates"

# Single-stage template: one slow stage (the main timeout victim)
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: slow-stage
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
    router:
      timeout_s: 120
      max_turns: 0
EOF

# Two-stage template: fast-one is instant; fast-two blocks for a long time
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-two-stage.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-two-stage
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: fast-one
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
  - id: fast-two
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Always-run (release + persist) template: flow stage + always_run release + persist
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-with-release.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-with-release
extends: simple
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release
  - persist-stage

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

persist-stage:
  gate: auto
  roles: [persist]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Commit the templates into the overlay repo so the runner can find them
(cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add timeout test templates") >/dev/null 2>&1

# ── P1: basic timeout — slow stage, status=timed_out ───────────────────────

# Stage that sleeps far longer than max_run_s
mock_plugin_factory "slow-stage" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
SLOW_STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/slow-stage-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    sleep 120
    $(mock_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR"
print_test_section "P1: slow stage timeout — status=timed_out written to pipeline-state.json"

# Run with ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 (2 seconds); wrap in timeout 25s to prevent hanging
# before implementation (no watchdog → stage sleeps forever → outer timeout kills it)
p1_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p1" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stderr" \
    || p1_rc=$?

STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

# Runner must exit non-zero (timed-out runs are failures)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p1_rc"

# pipeline-state.json must exist and have status=timed_out
if [[ ! -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
else
    _p1_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p1_status"
fi

print_test_section "P1: pipeline.end event fields — status=timed_out, stage, limit_s"

if [[ ! -f "$EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: events.jsonl written" "events file not found"
else
    # Event: pipeline.end with status=timed_out
    _p1_end_event="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out")' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_end_event" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted" \
            "no such event in $(wc -l < "$EVENTS_JSONL") events"
    fi

    # The event must carry the in-flight stage name
    _p1_stage="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_stage" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage (stage=$_p1_stage)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage" \
            "stage field empty in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi

    # The event must carry limit_s (the max_run_s value that was applied)
    _p1_limit="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.limit_s // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_limit" && "$_p1_limit" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s=$_p1_limit"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s" \
            "limit_s field absent or non-numeric in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi
fi

# ── P2: idle between dispatches — watchdog fires independently of stage state ─
print_test_section "P2: watchdog fires even when engine is idle between dispatches"

# Reset state/events for fresh run
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"
mock_plugin_factory "fast-one" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "fast-two" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

# fast-one: returns immediately (proves it can complete BEFORE the watchdog fires)
# fast-two: sleeps 30s (watchdog fires during fast-two's execution)
# max_run_s=3: watchdog fires 3s into the run. fast-one completes in < 1s.
# After 3s, fast-one's status in pipeline-state.json MUST be "complete", proving
# the watchdog ran independently — it did not need a stage to be dispatching.
# If the watchdog fired BEFORE fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be
# "complete", and the assertion below would fail.
FAST_TWO_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fast-two-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-one/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_one_run() {
    $(mock_result_line fast-one)
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-two/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_two_run() {
    : > "${FAST_TWO_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_result_line fast-two)
    return 0
}
PLUG

p2_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-two-stage --goal "run-timed-out test p2" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stderr" \
    || p2_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p2_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p2_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline status=timed_out (watchdog fires regardless of dispatch state)" \
        "timed_out" "$_p2_status"

    # fast-one MUST have completed before the watchdog fired: its status must be
    # "complete". This is the falsifiable check — if the watchdog fired before
    # fast-one completed, fast-one's status would not be "complete" and this fails.
    # Stage names are stored with their literal name (hyphenated) as the key.
    _p2_fast_one="$(jq -r '.stage_statuses["fast-one"] // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_p2_fast_one" == "complete" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired (watchdog fires independently)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired" \
            "fast-one status: '${_p2_fast_one:-<empty>}' — watchdog fired too early or fast-one did not run"
    fi
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

# ── P3: TERM-ignore → KILL within TERM + 10s ────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "P3: stage that ignores SIGTERM is dead within TERM + 10s"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

# Stage that traps SIGTERM and does NOT exit, sleeps indefinitely
TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/term-ignore-pid"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    # Record our PID so the test can check it is dead
    printf '%s\n' "\$\$" > "${TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE}"
    # Trap SIGTERM and ignore it (only SIGKILL can stop this)
    trap '' TERM
    sleep 120
    $(mock_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

_p3_start="$(date +%s)"
# max_run_s=2 → watchdog fires at 2s, sends TERM; stage ignores it;
# watchdog escalates to KILL at 2+10=12s. The runner must exit within ~15s.
p3_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 30 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p3 term-ignore" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stderr" \
    || p3_rc=$?
_p3_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _p3_start ))

# Runner must exit (not hang past 30s timeout)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits non-zero (not still running)" "1" "$p3_rc"

# Runner must exit within TERM + 10s + buffer = 2 + 10 + 5 = 17s
if [[ "$_p3_elapsed" -le 17 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer (elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer" \
        "elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s > 17s"
fi

# If stage PID was written, check the process is dead
if [[ -f "$TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE" ]]; then
    _ignore_pid="$(cat "$TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_ignore_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        if kill -0 "$_ignore_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: TERM-ignoring stage process is dead after TERM+10s" \
                "PID $_ignore_pid is still alive"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: TERM-ignoring stage process is dead (PID $_ignore_pid killed)"
        fi
    fi
fi

# ── P4: release AND persist stages run on timed-out exit path ───────────────
print_test_section "P4: always_run release and persist stages execute on timed-out exit path"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

mock_plugin_factory "outcome"       "agent" 0 "" ""        >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown"      "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "persist-stage" "tool"  0 "" "persist"  >/dev/null

# Outcome (flow) stage: sleeps 30s (will be killed by watchdog)
OUTCOME_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/outcome-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "${OUTCOME_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_result_line outcome)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Release (teardown) stage: drops a marker to prove it ran
RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran-on-timeout"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    $(mock_result_line teardown)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Persist stage: drops a marker to prove it ran
PERSIST_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/persist-ran-on-timeout"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/persist-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
persist_stage_run() {
    : > "${PERSIST_MARKER}"
    $(mock_result_line persist-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

p4_rc=0
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-with-release --goal "run-timed-out test p4 release+persist" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p4.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p4.stderr" \
    || p4_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: runner exits non-zero on timed-out path" "1" "$p4_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p4_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: pipeline status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p4_status"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

if [[ -e "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: release (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: release (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path" \
        "release marker not found — always_run release stage did not execute"
fi

if [[ -e "$PERSIST_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: persist (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: persist (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path" \
        "persist marker not found — always_run persist stage did not execute"
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh — run-level wall-clock limit (#1944)
3	#
4	# SPEC-2 [code]:
5	#   _runner_resolve_run_limit_s resolves template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S >
6	#   20700; a non-integer or non-positive value in template or env yields
7	#   disposition misconfigured and the run does not reach the dispatch loop.
8	#
9	# SPEC-5 [no-code]:
10	#   The limit is resolved from template, env, or constant only; scripts/lib/
11	#   stage-limits.sh and core/pipeline/runner.sh contain no reference to
12	#   GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI, or any platform-specific variable in the new code.
13	#
14	# SPEC-6 [no-code]:
15	#   ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary with ## Enforced by entries
16	#   citing the new tests; ADR-054 gains a §11 for the run-level limit with

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh — run-level wall-clock limit (#1944)
#
# SPEC-2 [code]:
#   _runner_resolve_run_limit_s resolves template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S >
#   20700; a non-integer or non-positive value in template or env yields
#   disposition misconfigured and the run does not reach the dispatch loop.
#
# SPEC-5 [no-code]:
#   The limit is resolved from template, env, or constant only; scripts/lib/
#   stage-limits.sh and core/pipeline/runner.sh contain no reference to
#   GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI, or any platform-specific variable in the new code.
#
# SPEC-6 [no-code]:
#   ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary with ## Enforced by entries
#   citing the new tests; ADR-054 gains a §11 for the run-level limit with
#   ## Enforced by; config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt no longer lists
#   ADR-054-stage-contract.md.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-limit-precedence: max_run_s resolution + platform-free + ADR alignment (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-limit-precedence"

RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
STAGE_LIMITS="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"

# ─── SPEC-2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s ────────────────────────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
source "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence: template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S > 20700"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Case 1: no template value, no env → falls back to default 20700
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] no template, no env → default 20700" "20700" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"

    # Case 2: env only → uses env
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] env ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600 used when no template value" "3600" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 3: template value > env → template wins
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '7200'; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S" "7200" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 4: template value only (no env) → template wins over default
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '1800'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over default" "1800" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer / non-positive → misconfigured, rc=1"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Non-integer in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf 'not-a-number'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-positive (zero) in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '0'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Negative in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf -- '-5'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] negative template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-integer in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="thirty"
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Non-positive in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] validation checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

# ─── SPEC-2: template_max_run_s() from the real template.sh ─────────────────
# This section sources the REAL template.sh to test its template_max_run_s()
# function directly. If template.sh is reverted (function removed), the
# assert_fail below fires — making template.sh testable.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() reads max_run_s from template YAML (real function)"
TEMPLATE_SH="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$TEMPLATE_SH" 2>/dev/null || true

# Build two YAML fixtures: one WITH max_run_s, one WITHOUT
_tpl_yaml="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/max-run-test.yaml"
cat > "$_tpl_yaml" <<'EOF'
id: max-run-test
max_run_s: 3600
extends: simple
EOF

_tpl_none="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/no-max-run.yaml"
cat > "$_tpl_none" <<'EOF'
id: no-max-run-test
extends: simple
EOF

if declare -F template_max_run_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Real function from template.sh: must extract the value from the YAML.
    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$_tpl_yaml"
    _tmr="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() returns max_run_s value from YAML" "3600" "$_tmr"

    # When max_run_s is absent, function returns empty (no override)
    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$_tpl_none"
    _tmr_empty="$(template_max_run_s 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() returns empty when max_run_s absent" "" "$_tmr_empty"
    unset _TPL_SOURCE_FILE
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] template_max_run_s() defined in core/pipeline/template.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing template.sh — implementation missing or template.sh reverted"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] misconfigured run (invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S): runner rejects before dispatch"
# Run the actual runner with an invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S; it must exit non-zero
# before dispatching any stage (no stage marker written).
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-miscfg"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-miscfg"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# Minimal single-stage plugin
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

MISCFG_OVERLAY="$(setup_git_temp_repo miscfg-run-limit)"
mkdir -p "$MISCFG_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates"
cat > "$MISCFG_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/limit-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: limit-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

STAGE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-ran-marker"
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
intake_run() {
    : > "${STAGE_MARKER}"
    $(mock_result_line intake)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Run with invalid env var — must fail before dispatch loop
_miscfg_rc=0
( cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="not-a-number" bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template limit-single --goal "test misconfigured limit" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stderr" \
    || _miscfg_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → runner exits non-zero" "1" "$_miscfg_rc"
if [[ -e "$STAGE_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when env limit is misconfigured" \
        "stage marker exists — dispatch loop was reached"
else
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when env limit is misconfigured"
fi

# Check that misconfigured is explained AND names the source (ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S)
_miscfg_sf="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
if [[ -f "$_miscfg_sf" ]]; then
    _miscfg_disp="$(jq -r '.disposition // empty' "$_miscfg_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] pipeline-state.json disposition=misconfigured (env)" "misconfigured" "$_miscfg_disp"
fi
# Collect output: prefer state file reason field, fall back to stderr+stdout
_miscfg_all_output=""
if [[ -f "$_miscfg_sf" ]]; then
    _miscfg_all_output="$(jq -r '.reason // .message // empty' "$_miscfg_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [[ -z "$_miscfg_all_output" ]]; then
    _miscfg_all_output="$(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stderr" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stdout" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
# The message must name the misconfigured source: ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
if grep -q 'ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S' <<< "$_miscfg_all_output" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] message names the misconfigured env source (ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] message names the misconfigured env source (ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S)" \
        "ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S not found in runner output — message must name the env source"
fi

# ─── SPEC-2 (template layer): runner rejects invalid template max_run_s ──────
# A template that contains `max_run_s: not-a-number` must make the runner
# abort with rc=1 before any stage dispatches. This exercises template.sh's
# template_max_run_s() function, which is called by _runner_resolve_run_limit_s.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] misconfigured run (invalid template max_run_s): runner rejects before dispatch"

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-miscfg-tpl"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-miscfg-tpl"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

# Template with an invalid max_run_s value in the YAML.
# MUST use new-shape (flow: style): the old-shape merger strips top-level keys
# like max_run_s: when building the merged file (only stages:/stage_definitions:
# blocks are carried over from the per-repo file). New-shape copies the file
# verbatim, so max_run_s: not-a-number survives in _TPL_SOURCE_FILE.
cat > "$MISCFG_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/limit-bad-tpl.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: limit-bad-tpl
extends: simple
max_run_s: not-a-number
flow:
  - intake

intake:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
EOF
(cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add limit-bad-tpl template") \
    >/dev/null 2>&1

STAGE_MARKER_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-ran-marker-tpl"
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
intake_run() {
    : > "${STAGE_MARKER_TPL}"
    $(mock_result_line intake)
    return 0
}
PLUG

_miscfg_tpl_rc=0
( cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template limit-bad-tpl --goal "test misconfigured template limit" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg-tpl.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg-tpl.stderr" \
    || _miscfg_tpl_rc=$?

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] invalid template max_run_s → runner exits non-zero" "1" "$_miscfg_tpl_rc"
if [[ -e "$STAGE_MARKER_TPL" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when template limit is misconfigured" \
        "stage marker exists — dispatch loop was reached"
else
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when template limit is misconfigured"
fi

# Message must name the misconfigured template source (max_run_s)
_miscfg_tpl_sf="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
_miscfg_tpl_output=""
if [[ -f "$_miscfg_tpl_sf" ]]; then
    _miscfg_tpl_output="$(jq -r '.reason // .message // empty' "$_miscfg_tpl_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
if [[ -z "$_miscfg_tpl_output" ]]; then
    _miscfg_tpl_output="$(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg-tpl.stderr" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg-tpl.stdout" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi
# max_run_s is the template YAML field name — the message must name the source
if grep -q 'max_run_s' <<< "$_miscfg_tpl_output" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] message names the misconfigured template source (max_run_s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] message names the misconfigured template source (max_run_s)" \
        "max_run_s not found in runner output — message must name the template source"
fi

# ─── SPEC-5: no platform-specific env vars in new limit code ────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh contains no GITHUB_ACTIONS or bare CI reference"

# GITHUB_ACTIONS check — never acceptable in limit resolution
_ga_count_sl="$(grep -c 'GITHUB_ACTIONS' "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh: no GITHUB_ACTIONS reference" "0" "$_ga_count_sl"

# $CI or ${CI} in non-comment code lines in stage-limits.sh
_ci_sl="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '\$\{?CI\}?[^A-Za-z0-9_]' || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh: no bare \$CI in non-comment code" "0" "$_ci_sl"

# runner.sh: no GITHUB_ACTIONS in code lines (excluding pure comments)
_ga_rn="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'GITHUB_ACTIONS' || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] runner.sh: no GITHUB_ACTIONS in code lines" "0" "$_ga_rn"

# runner.sh: no bare $CI in non-comment code lines
_ci_rn="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '\$\{?CI\}?[^A-Za-z0-9_]' || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] runner.sh: no bare \$CI in non-comment code" "0" "$_ci_rn"

# Additional platform-specific variables — none should appear in limit-resolution code
for _plat_var in TRAVIS CIRCLECI RUNNER_OS BUILD_BUILDID; do
    _cnt_sl="$(grep -c "$_plat_var" "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh: no $_plat_var reference" "0" "$_cnt_sl"
    _cnt_rn="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null | grep -c "$_plat_var" || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] runner.sh: no $_plat_var in code lines" "0" "$_cnt_rn"
done

# ─── SPEC-6: ADR alignment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary"
ADR025="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-025-abort-propagation.md"

if [[ ! -f "$ADR025" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 file exists" "not found: $ADR025"
else
    # The word vocabulary line lists the abort words; timed_out must be among them
    _vocab_line="$(grep -E '(sigint|sigterm|cycle_abort).*timed_out|timed_out.*(sigint|sigterm|cycle_abort)' \
        "$ADR025" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_vocab_line" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 word vocabulary includes timed_out"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 word vocabulary includes timed_out" \
            "timed_out not found alongside sigint/sigterm/cycle_abort in ADR-025"
    fi

    # ## Enforced by section must cite the new test files
    _enf_sec="$(awk '/^## Enforced by/,0' "$ADR025" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if grep -q "run-timed-out-test\|run-limit-precedence-test\|run-watchdog-clean-exit-test\|resume-after-run-timeout-test" \
            <<< "$_enf_sec" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 ## Enforced by cites new tests"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 ## Enforced by cites new tests" \
            "none of the new test files referenced in ## Enforced by"
    fi
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054 has §11 for run-level limit with ## Enforced by"
ADR054="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md"

if [[ ! -f "$ADR054" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054 file exists" "not found: $ADR054"
else
    # §11 must exist (run-level limit section)
    if grep -qE '§[[:space:]]*11\b|###[[:space:]]+11\.' "$ADR054" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054 §11 exists"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054 §11 exists" \
            "no §11 heading found in ADR-054"
    fi

    # §11 area must have an ## Enforced by entry citing a run-limit test
    _adr054_enf="$(awk '/## Enforced by/,0' "$ADR054" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if grep -q "run-limit-precedence-test\|run-timed-out-test\|run-watchdog-clean-exit-test\|resume-after-run-timeout-test" \
            <<< "$_adr054_enf" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054 ## Enforced by cites run-limit tests"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054 ## Enforced by cites run-limit tests" \
            "no run-limit test referenced in ADR-054 ## Enforced by"
    fi
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt does not list ADR-054-stage-contract.md"
BASELINE="$REPO_ROOT/config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"

if [[ ! -f "$BASELINE" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] adr-enforcement-baseline.txt exists" "not found: $BASELINE"
else
    if grep -q 'ADR-054-stage-contract\.md' "$BASELINE" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054-stage-contract.md removed from baseline" \
            "still listed in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-054-stage-contract.md removed from baseline"
    fi
fi

# ─── SPEC-6: run_end_words knows timed_out (run-open-items.sh) ──────────────
# run-open-items.sh adds timed_out to run_end_words. If reverted, the
# timed_out case falls through to a generic message that does not mention the
# wall-clock limit, and the assertion fails.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] run_end_words timed_out describes the wall-clock limit"
RUN_OPEN_ITEMS="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh
source "$RUN_OPEN_ITEMS" 2>/dev/null || true

if declare -F run_end_words >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _to_words="$(run_end_words timed_out 0 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if grep -qi 'wall-clock' <<< "$_to_words" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-6] run_end_words timed_out describes the wall-clock limit"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] run_end_words timed_out describes the wall-clock limit" \
            "got: '${_to_words:-<empty>}' — timed_out case missing from run_end_words"
    fi
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] run_end_words defined in run-open-items.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing run-open-items.sh"
fi

# ─── SPEC-6: lint-adr-enforced-by passes ────────────────────────────────────
# Verifies every ## Enforced by citation in all ADRs (including ADR-025 and
# ADR-054) references a real file. Passes after this change (new test files
# exist); would fail if an ADR cited a test that did not exist yet.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] lint-adr-enforced-by: all Enforced-by citations resolve"
_adr_lint_rc=0
bash "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/lint-adr-enforced-by.sh" \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/adr-lint.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/adr-lint.stderr" \
    || _adr_lint_rc=$?
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-6] lint-adr-enforced-by passes (ADR citations all resolve)" \
    "0" "$_adr_lint_rc"

# ADR-025: Abort Propagation Contract

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Accepted:** 2026-06-04 (Wave 15-B #684 ships the helpers + dispatch-site conversion)
**Depends on:** ADR-006 (resume contract), ADR-024 (subprocess env isolation — sentinel-file precedent)
**Implemented by:** #684 (Wave 15-B impl: helper + dispatch-site conversion). Umbrella: #679.

## Context

Three consecutive discoveries of the same abort-propagation bug class —
each at a different dispatch site — have shipped tactical per-site fixes
that did not generalize:

1. **#612 (Wave 8)** — `route_to_model_loop` did not distinguish a
   SIGINT-driven child exit (rc=130) from a generic per-iteration failure
   and continued the loop, spawning another iteration after the user
   hit Ctrl-C. Tactical fix at `core/router/route.sh:527-539, 636, 841-863`
   installed an INT/TERM trap that captures the child pid, signals it,
   and surfaces rc=130 from the loop so the caller can propagate.
   The trap installer (`_route_loop_install_traps`) and signal
   handler (`_route_loop_on_signal`) are the per-site primitives.
2. **#616 (Wave 8)** — same bug class one layer up: the build plugin
   captured rc=130 from the router but then ran post-processing as if the
   call had succeeded, returning rc=0 to the runner. Tactical fix added an
   explicit `[[ $rc -eq 130 ]] && return 130` check after each router
   call. The runner's `_runner_signal_trap` at `core/pipeline/runner.sh:863-872`
   was added to convert SIGINT into a clean rc=130 exit and trigger the
   abort EXIT trap.
3. **Wave 15 dogfood `20260604061056-1003` (this ADR's motivating
   discovery)** — the cycle orchestrator (introduced by ADR-021 *after*
   Wave 8 shipped, so it never received the per-site SIGINT pattern) has
   the third instance of the same gap. `_cycle_iter_dispatch` at
   `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:664-681` captures `rc=$?` from
   `cycle_dispatch_stage`, increments `fail` if non-zero, and continues to
   the next stage. rc=130 looks indistinguishable from a normal stage
   failure. The cycle keeps spinning after the user hit Ctrl-C.

The pattern is now clear: every new dispatcher recreates the bug. Per-site
SIGINT handling is a treadmill — it patches the site that surfaced the
issue, not the class. The cycle orchestrator gap is the third instance;
the next dispatcher (strategy plugins, future orchestrators) is one
unchecked `rc=$?` away from re-discovery.

What's missing is a single semantic contract that tells dispatch-site
authors how to propagate abort across nested dispatch layers, plus a
cross-subshell signal channel for cases where rc propagation alone is too
slow (a child that hasn't returned yet when a sibling child sees the
abort).

## Decision

zBuild codifies a **two-layer abort propagation contract**. Every
dispatcher — runner, cycle orchestrator, future strategy plugins —
participates in both layers.

### Layer 1 — rc=130 propagation chokepoint helper
**(superseded 2026-10-08 by the #1850 amendment below — the abort is a recorded word; every helper returns 0 or 1)**

A single framework-owned helper, `_zbuild_propagate_abort`, lives in
`scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`. Signature:

```
_zbuild_propagate_abort <child_rc>
  returns <child_rc> if <child_rc> is an abort rc (130 today;
  130 or 143 once Wave 15-F #686 ships SIGTERM parity), else 0
```

The helper returns the abort rc it was given, not a hard-coded 130.
This means the SIGTERM widening in #686 is a one-line change to the
helper's classifier (add 143 to the recognised set) and does not change
the helper's signature or the call-site contract. Every dispatcher calls
it immediately after capturing each child rc. Greppable —
`grep -r _zbuild_propagate_abort` enumerates every dispatch site
participating in the contract. Single point to evolve when SIGTERM parity
ships.

### Layer 2 — sentinel file `${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal`

content.content:
`pipeline.aborted reason=sigint status=interrupted`. ADR-025 adds the
sentinel-file cleanup: the EXIT trap removes
`${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal` after emitting the event, so a
subsequent `zbuild` invocation in the same state dir does not see a stale
sentinel.

Trap composition is **additive**, not clobbering. The Wave 15-B impl
must compose the sentinel-creation step onto the existing
`_runner_signal_trap` body (which already calls `exit 130`) and the
sentinel-removal step onto the existing `_runner_abort_trap` EXIT body —
not replace them. This matches the ADR-024 amendment's additive-trap
discipline for the test harness.

## SIGTERM extension
**(superseded 2026-10-08 by the #1850 amendment below — the abort is a recorded word; every helper returns 0 or 1)**

ADR-025 anticipates rc=143 (128 + SIGTERM) carrying the same semantics
as rc=130. The `_zbuild_propagate_abort` helper returns the abort rc it
was given (not a hard-coded 130), so widening to rc=143 is a one-line
change to the helper's internal classifier and leaves the signature,
the call-site contract, and the sentinel-file pathway unchanged. The
sentinel file is signal-agnostic — any abort cause writes the same
sentinel. This ADR scopes the contract to SIGINT for now; #686 widens
it without changing the helper signatures or call-site contract.

## Member dispatch sites

Current call sites being modified by Wave 15-B (#684):

- `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh` — `_cycle_iter_dispatch` at
  `:664-681` (the dogfood bug). Adds pre-flight `_zbuild_check_abort`
  before `cycle_dispatch_stage`, post-flight `_zbuild_propagate_abort`
  after capturing `rc=$?`.
- `core/pipeline/runner.sh` — linear stage loop already honors rc=130
  via the existing #612/#616 pattern. Adds the sentinel pre-flight
  `_zbuild_check_abort` before each stage dispatch for parity with the
  cycle orchestrator, plus the sentinel-write step in
  `_runner_signal_trap` and sentinel-remove step in `_runner_abort_trap`.
- `core/router/route.sh` — `route_to_model_loop`'s per-iter body at
  `:527-539, 636, 841-863` already returns 130 on signal. Converts the
  ad-hoc trap-and-kill primitives to call the new helpers on the
  post-spawn rc path. Pre-flight sentinel check before each
  `claude` exec spawn.

Future candidates:

- Strategy plugins that fan out child dispatches (e.g., parallel-
  candidate strategies).
- Future orchestrators (compound-quality loop, retry orchestrator).
- Any plugin whose body contains a `for stage in ...; do dispatch; done`
  shape.
--
- One more piece of framework vocabulary (`_zbuild_propagate_abort`,
  `_zbuild_check_abort`) that dispatch-site authors must learn.
  Mitigated by the helpers living in one file with the contract
  colocated.
- Additive trap composition needs care: the Wave 15-B impl must compose
  onto existing `_runner_signal_trap` / `_runner_abort_trap` bodies,
  not replace them. A reviewer checklist item.
- Sentinel file is filesystem state; a crashed runner that did not run
  its EXIT trap leaves a stale sentinel. Mitigated by the next runner
  invocation observing rc=130 immediately and surfacing a clear error
  (or, with a pre-flight clean step at runner entry, removing the
  stale file).

**Open follow-ups:**

- **Wave 15-B (#684)** — ship `_zbuild_propagate_abort` +
  `_zbuild_check_abort` in `scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`, convert
  the three dispatch sites (cycle orchestrator, runner, router), add
  the runner's sentinel-write/remove steps. ADR-025 flips from
  Proposed to Accepted on that merge.
- **Wave 15-E (#685)** — resume contract integration: a run aborted via
  SIGINT writes resume metadata before the EXIT trap exits, so the user
  can `zbuild resume` from the aborted stage. Builds on ADR-006.
- **Wave 15-F (#686)** — SIGTERM parity. Widens the helpers to accept
  rc=143 and routes SIGTERM through the same trap composition.
- **Wave 15-G (#687)** — faster pre-abort: poll the sentinel from
  long-running stages (not just at dispatch boundaries) so SIGINT is
  honored mid-stage rather than at the next stage boundary.
- **Wave 15-H (#688)** — reconsider process-group signal forwarding
  (alternative b) once helper baseline is in place.

## Amendment (#905, 2026-06-15) — the loop signal handler reaps synchronously

Wave 15-G (#687) gave `_route_loop_on_signal` a process-group kill: TERM the
whole group, then escalate to SIGKILL after a 1s grace so a trap-ignoring or
wedged claude still dies. That escalation was **detached** — scheduled as
`{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL -- -PGID; } &` and `disown`ed — and the handler
returned 130 immediately. claude routinely ignores/delays SIGTERM, so in
practice the child is only ever reaped by that detached backstop ~1s later,
*after* `route_to_model_loop` has already returned and its caller/driver has
unwound and exited. The backstop is then an orphan racing the caller's
teardown; the SIGKILL can land late, or be lost entirely if the orphan is
reaped before its `sleep` elapses. The observable failure was orphaned claude
processes surviving an abort — a flaky `route-fast-abort-test.sh` leak under
CI load.

**Amended contract: the loop signal handler aborts synchronously.**
`_route_loop_on_signal` MUST NOT return until the child tree it signalled has
actually been reaped. The implementation keeps the TERM→grace→KILL escalation
but runs the SIGKILL grace in a **local watchdog that the handler itself reaps**,
and `wait`s on the child before returning:
--
ADR-054 §4 makes exit codes binary everywhere, the engine's own paths included. This ADR's two layers carried the abort *as* an rc (130, then 143, and later 6, 9 and 10 joined), and every reader mapped those numbers its own way — `cycle_orchestrator_run` collapsed a nested `cycle_abort` into `config_invalid` (#1860). The layers stay; what they carry changes.

- **An abort is recorded once, as a word:** `sigint`, `sigterm`, `cycle_abort`, `llm_unavailable`, `llm_rate_limited`, `scope_too_large`, or `timed_out`. It is held in the process (`_ZB_ABORT_REASON`) and written into the sentinel `${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal`, which still crosses subshells and env scrubs (ADR-024). The first recorded abort wins. An empty sentinel reads as `sigint`. The run-level watchdog writes `timed_out` before sending SIGTERM to the process group; first-wins preserves `timed_out` over the `sigterm` that the runner's signal trap would otherwise record.
- **The helpers return 0 or 1.** `_zbuild_abort <word>` records and returns 1; `_zbuild_abort_reason` reads the word back (from the sentinel when this process has none); `_zbuild_check_abort` is 1 when an abort is recorded; `_zbuild_propagate_abort <rc>` is 1 only when the child failed *and* an abort is recorded. `_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel [word]` records (default `sigint`); disarming clears both channels.
- **Every signal handler records the word:** the runner's (`_runner_signal_trap`), the cycle's (`_cycle_on_signal`) and the parallel group's (`_parallel_on_signal`). An `abort_when` match records `cycle_abort`; an unavailable model records `llm_unavailable` / `llm_rate_limited`.
- **The runner ends on the word**, in one place (`_runner_end_on_abort`): `sigint` / `sigterm` / `cycle_abort` → status `interrupted`; `llm_unavailable` / `llm_rate_limited` / `scope_too_large` → status `aborted`. `pipeline.aborted` carries the word as its reason. The process exits 1 — the signal is in that reason, not in 130 or 143.

The dispatch-site contract is unchanged in shape: pre-flight `_zbuild_check_abort || return 1`, post-flight `_zbuild_propagate_abort $? || return 1`.

## Enforced by

- Decision, both layers (#1850: the abort is recorded once as a word, in-process and in the sentinel; the first wins; every helper returns 0 or 1; no state dir → in-process only) → `tests/unit/abort-propagation-test.sh` A1–A9
- Dispatch site contract — the cycle orchestrator (pre-flight before each member, post-flight after a leaf; the signal handler records the word; a leaf abort ends the loop `aborted` with its reason) → `tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-orchestrator-run-test.sh` T9, T14
- Dispatch site contract — the parallel group (a signal kills the in-flight members, records its word, and the group returns 1) → `tests/integration/parallel-orchestrator-test.sh` T4
- #1850 (the runner ends on the word: status and `pipeline.aborted` reason per word; `main` returns 1) → `tests/unit/runner-cycle-rc-action-mapping-test.sh`
- No engine path returns or reads an abort rc (130, 143, 6, 9, 10) → `tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh` SPEC-1, SPEC-16
- Dispatch site contract — the pre-flight sits at the hook call itself, in both dispatch boundaries (a retry after a wait, and each parallel member, never start once an abort is recorded) → `tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh` SPEC-17
- Cleanup contract (the EXIT trap clears the sentinel; `pipeline.aborted reason=sigint` on Ctrl-C) → `tests/integration/full-pipeline-sigint-test.sh`
- SIGTERM extension (`reason=sigterm`) → `tests/integration/sigterm-aborts-pipeline-test.sh`
- Resume clears a stale sentinel before the first pre-flight → `tests/integration/resume-after-sigint-test.sh`
- Run-level watchdog writes `timed_out`; first-wins preserves it over the runner's `sigterm` write; pipeline ends `timed_out`, watchdog fires between dispatches, TERM-ignoring stage reaped within TERM+10 s, always-run stages execute → `tests/integration/run-timed-out-test.sh`
- `timed_out` in the word vocabulary; limit resolution precedence and misconfigured validation → `tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh`
- Watchdog reaped on clean exit; pipeline status unchanged after clean run → `tests/unit/run-watchdog-clean-exit-test.sh`
- Resume after `timed_out`: `get_resume_recommendation` returns `manual_resume_only`; fresh watchdog armed on resume → `tests/integration/resume-after-run-timeout-test.sh`

## References

- [ADR-006](ADR-006-resume-contract.md) — resume contract; aborted runs
  MAY be resumable, integrated by Wave 15-E (#685).
- [ADR-024](ADR-024-subprocess-env-isolation.md) — subprocess env
  isolation; the sentinel-file pattern is the cross-subshell signal

- Issue #679 (this ADR) — Wave 15-A umbrella.

sentinel-file cleanup: the EXIT trap removes
`${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal` after emitting the event, so a
subsequent `zbuild` invocation in the same state dir does not see a stale
sentinel.

Trap composition is **additive**, not clobbering. The Wave 15-B impl
must compose the sentinel-creation step onto the existing
`_runner_signal_trap` body (which already calls `exit 130`) and the
sentinel-removal step onto the existing `_runner_abort_trap` EXIT body —
not replace them. This matches the ADR-024 amendment's additive-trap
discipline for the test harness.

## SIGTERM extension
**(superseded 2026-10-08 by the #1850 amendment below — the abort is a recorded word; every helper returns 0 or 1)**

ADR-025 anticipates rc=143 (128 + SIGTERM) carrying the same semantics
as rc=130. The `_zbuild_propagate_abort` helper returns the abort rc it
was given (not a hard-coded 130), so widening to rc=143 is a one-line
change to the helper's internal classifier and leaves the signature,
the call-site contract, and the sentinel-file pathway unchanged. The
sentinel file is signal-agnostic — any abort cause writes the same
sentinel. This ADR scopes the contract to SIGINT for now; #686 widens
it without changing the helper signatures or call-site contract.

## Member dispatch sites

Current call sites being modified by Wave 15-B (#684):

- `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh` — `_cycle_iter_dispatch` at
  `:664-681` (the dogfood bug). Adds pre-flight `_zbuild_check_abort`
  before `cycle_dispatch_stage`, post-flight `_zbuild_propagate_abort`
  after capturing `rc=$?`.
- `core/pipeline/runner.sh` — linear stage loop already honors rc=130
  via the existing #612/#616 pattern. Adds the sentinel pre-flight
  `_zbuild_check_abort` before each stage dispatch for parity with the
  cycle orchestrator, plus the sentinel-write step in
  `_runner_signal_trap` and sentinel-remove step in `_runner_abort_trap`.
- `core/router/route.sh` — `route_to_model_loop`'s per-iter body at
  `:527-539, 636, 841-863` already returns 130 on signal. Converts the
  ad-hoc trap-and-kill primitives to call the new helpers on the
  post-spawn rc path. Pre-flight sentinel check before each
  `claude` exec spawn.

Future candidates:

- Strategy plugins that fan out child dispatches (e.g., parallel-
  candidate strategies).
- Future orchestrators (compound-quality loop, retry orchestrator).
- Any plugin whose body contains a `for stage in ...; do dispatch; done`
  shape.
--
- One more piece of framework vocabulary (`_zbuild_propagate_abort`,
  `_zbuild_check_abort`) that dispatch-site authors must learn.
  Mitigated by the helpers living in one file with the contract
  colocated.
- Additive trap composition needs care: the Wave 15-B impl must compose
  onto existing `_runner_signal_trap` / `_runner_abort_trap` bodies,
  not replace them. A reviewer checklist item.
- Sentinel file is filesystem state; a crashed runner that did not run
  its EXIT trap leaves a stale sentinel. Mitigated by the next runner
  invocation observing rc=130 immediately and surfacing a clear error
  (or, with a pre-flight clean step at runner entry, removing the
  stale file).

**Open follow-ups:**

- **Wave 15-B (#684)** — ship `_zbuild_propagate_abort` +
  `_zbuild_check_abort` in `scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`, convert
  the three dispatch sites (cycle orchestrator, runner, router), add
  the runner's sentinel-write/remove steps. ADR-025 flips from
  Proposed to Accepted on that merge.
- **Wave 15-E (#685)** — resume contract integration: a run aborted via
  SIGINT writes resume metadata before the EXIT trap exits, so the user
  can `zbuild resume` from the aborted stage. Builds on ADR-006.
- **Wave 15-F (#686)** — SIGTERM parity. Widens the helpers to accept
  rc=143 and routes SIGTERM through the same trap composition.
- **Wave 15-G (#687)** — faster pre-abort: poll the sentinel from
  long-running stages (not just at dispatch boundaries) so SIGINT is
  honored mid-stage rather than at the next stage boundary.
- **Wave 15-H (#688)** — reconsider process-group signal forwarding
  (alternative b) once helper baseline is in place.

## Amendment (#905, 2026-06-15) — the loop signal handler reaps synchronously

Wave 15-G (#687) gave `_route_loop_on_signal` a process-group kill: TERM the
whole group, then escalate to SIGKILL after a 1s grace so a trap-ignoring or
wedged claude still dies. That escalation was **detached** — scheduled as
`{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL -- -PGID; } &` and `disown`ed — and the handler
returned 130 immediately. claude routinely ignores/delays SIGTERM, so in
practice the child is only ever reaped by that detached backstop ~1s later,
*after* `route_to_model_loop` has already returned and its caller/driver has
unwound and exited. The backstop is then an orphan racing the caller's
teardown; the SIGKILL can land late, or be lost entirely if the orphan is
reaped before its `sleep` elapses. The observable failure was orphaned claude
processes surviving an abort — a flaky `route-fast-abort-test.sh` leak under
CI load.

**Amended contract: the loop signal handler aborts synchronously.**
`_route_loop_on_signal` MUST NOT return until the child tree it signalled has
actually been reaped. The implementation keeps the TERM→grace→KILL escalation
but runs the SIGKILL grace in a **local watchdog that the handler itself reaps**,
and `wait`s on the child before returning:
--
ADR-054 §4 makes exit codes binary everywhere, the engine's own paths included. This ADR's two layers carried the abort *as* an rc (130, then 143, and later 6, 9 and 10 joined), and every reader mapped those numbers its own way — `cycle_orchestrator_run` collapsed a nested `cycle_abort` into `config_invalid` (#1860). The layers stay; what they carry changes.

- **An abort is recorded once, as a word:** `sigint`, `sigterm`, `cycle_abort`, `llm_unavailable`, `llm_rate_limited`, `scope_too_large`, or `timed_out`. It is held in the process (`_ZB_ABORT_REASON`) and written into the sentinel `${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal`, which still crosses subshells and env scrubs (ADR-024). The first recorded abort wins. An empty sentinel reads as `sigint`. The run-level watchdog writes `timed_out` before sending SIGTERM to the process group; first-wins preserves `timed_out` over the `sigterm` that the runner's signal trap would otherwise record.
- **The helpers return 0 or 1.** `_zbuild_abort <word>` records and returns 1; `_zbuild_abort_reason` reads the word back (from the sentinel when this process has none); `_zbuild_check_abort` is 1 when an abort is recorded; `_zbuild_propagate_abort <rc>` is 1 only when the child failed *and* an abort is recorded. `_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel [word]` records (default `sigint`); disarming clears both channels.
- **Every signal handler records the word:** the runner's (`_runner_signal_trap`), the cycle's (`_cycle_on_signal`) and the parallel group's (`_parallel_on_signal`). An `abort_when` match records `cycle_abort`; an unavailable model records `llm_unavailable` / `llm_rate_limited`.
- **The runner ends on the word**, in one place (`_runner_end_on_abort`): `sigint` / `sigterm` / `cycle_abort` → status `interrupted`; `llm_unavailable` / `llm_rate_limited` / `scope_too_large` → status `aborted`. `pipeline.aborted` carries the word as its reason. The process exits 1 — the signal is in that reason, not in 130 or 143.

The dispatch-site contract is unchanged in shape: pre-flight `_zbuild_check_abort || return 1`, post-flight `_zbuild_propagate_abort $? || return 1`.

## Enforced by

- Decision, both layers (#1850: the abort is recorded once as a word, in-process and in the sentinel; the first wins; every helper returns 0 or 1; no state dir → in-process only) → `tests/unit/abort-propagation-test.sh` A1–A9
- Dispatch site contract — the cycle orchestrator (pre-flight before each member, post-flight after a leaf; the signal handler records the word; a leaf abort ends the loop `aborted` with its reason) → `tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-orchestrator-run-test.sh` T9, T14

- #1850 (the runner ends on the word: status and `pipeline.aborted` reason per word; `main` returns 1) → `tests/unit/runner-cycle-rc-action-mapping-test.sh`

- Dispatch site contract — the pre-flight sits at the hook call itself, in both dispatch boundaries (a retry after a wait, and each parallel member, never start once an abort is recorded) → `tests/unit/dispatch-rc-guard-test.sh` SPEC-17
- Cleanup contract (the EXIT trap clears the sentinel; `pipeline.aborted reason=sigint` on Ctrl-C) → `tests/integration/full-pipeline-sigint-test.sh`
- SIGTERM extension (`reason=sigterm`) → `tests/integration/sigterm-aborts-pipeline-test.sh`

# is worse than leaving it stale, so this states the fact and stops. Best-effort
# throughout: it must never turn a failed run into a hung one, so every git call
# is bounded and non-fatal, and ZBUILD_ENGINE_DRIFT_CHECK=0 disables it outright.
_runner_report_engine_drift() {
    local reason="${1:-}"
    # Only the failures a newer engine could plausibly have changed. A terminal
    # abort (signal, llm_unavailable) is not one of them.
    case "$reason" in
        blocked_on_scope|max_iterations|blocked_on_gate) ;;
        *) return 0 ;;
    esac
    [[ "${ZBUILD_ENGINE_DRIFT_CHECK:-1}" == "1" ]] || return 0

    local sha="${_RUNNER_ENGINE_SHA:-}"
    [[ -n "$sha" && "$sha" != "unknown" ]] || return 0
    local root="${_ZBUILD_ROOT:-}"
    [[ -n "$root" ]] || return 0

    # `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns the literal "HEAD" on a detached
    # checkout — which the CI engine clone is. Left alone it would ask the remote
    # for its symbolic HEAD, which is usually right by accident and wrong the
    # moment the default branch is not main.
    local branch="${_RUNNER_ENGINE_BRANCH:-main}"
    [[ "$branch" == "unknown" || "$branch" == "HEAD" || -z "$branch" ]] && branch="main"

    # Remote tip, without mutating the frozen engine tree. Fully-qualified ref:
    # a bare name also matches refs/tags/<name>. A tag sharing a LIVE branch's
    # name is harmless (refs/heads sorts first), but a tag with NO matching
    # branch answers in its place — and then the drift check is comparing
    # against an object that is not a branch tip at all.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/dispatch.sh — plugin dispatch helpers extracted from runner.sh
# (issue #279). Resolves stage name → plugin directory via the registry.
# No behavior change from the original runner-embedded version.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# Depends on yaml_get and discover_plugins — both in
# core/plugin-registry/registry.sh. Re-source defensively if either is
# absent so the file is self-contained when tests source dispatch.sh
# directly. (Copilot caught on #280: yaml_get is NOT in helpers.sh.)
if ! declare -F yaml_get >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    source "$_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
fi

# _find_plugin_for_stage <stage> [plugins_root]
# Returns plugin directory path on stdout, exit 1 if no matching plugin found.
_find_plugin_for_stage() {
    local stage="$1" plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_ROOT/plugins}}" plugin_dir id
    local -a _fps_dirs=()
    discover_plugins_into _fps_dirs "$plugins_root"
    for plugin_dir in ${_fps_dirs[@]+"${_fps_dirs[@]}"}; do
        yaml_get_v id "$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml" "id"
        [[ "$id" == "$stage" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
    done
    return 1
}

# resolve_stage_plugin <stage> [plugins_root]
# ADR-042: uniform stage→plugin resolution. Adopted by the cycle and parallel
# dispatch paths (runner.sh) to match the leaf path's pre-existing role-then-id
# rule (the leaf path keeps its own inline logic). A stage's flow-name need not
# equal its plugin `id` — role binding (ADR-001) is resolved FIRST, with id-match
# as the backward-compat fallback. Cycle and parallel members previously used
# id-only and so silently failed to resolve role-bound stages whose plugin id ≠
# stage name (e.g. lint→lint-gate, lens-*→review-lens).
# Single-plugin resolution (cycle/parallel members do NOT fan out): first match
# wins. Side-effect-free: echoes the plugin dir and returns 0 on hit, returns 1
# if nothing resolves. (The resolver's best-effort registry.role-unresolved
# diagnostic on a role miss is the same as every other strategy path.)
resolve_stage_plugin() {
    local stage="$1" plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_ROOT/plugins}}"
    local roles role platform plugin_dir
    # Role-then-id: try declared roles first (when template data + resolver present).
    if declare -F template_stage_roles >/dev/null 2>&1 && declare -F resolve_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        roles="$(template_stage_roles "$stage" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [[ -n "$roles" ]]; then
            # Mirror fanout.sh ~41-43: platform-specific then generic. Use the
            # caller's detected platforms (dynamic scope from runner) when set;
            # the resolver itself falls back to generic plugins within one call.
            local -a _platforms=()
            if declare -p _DETECTED_PLATFORMS >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ${#_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
                _platforms=("${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}")
            fi
            while IFS= read -r role; do
                [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
                for platform in "${_platforms[@]+"${_platforms[@]}"}"; do
                    plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
                    [[ -n "$plugin_dir" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
                done
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
                [[ -n "$plugin_dir" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
            done <<< "$roles"
            # Fail-closed: roles were declared but none resolved — no id-match fallback.
            # Roles arrive newline-separated; substitute rather than word-split so a
            # role token containing a glob char cannot expand against the filesystem.
            printf 'resolve_stage_plugin: stage %s: unresolved declared roles: %s\n' \
                "$stage" "${roles//$'\n'/ }" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    # Fallback: backward-compat id match (stage name == manifest id).
    # Only reached when no roles are declared for this stage.
    plugin_dir="$(_find_plugin_for_stage "$stage" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$plugin_dir" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
    return 1

# compat if the marker is set but the reason was not recorded (a path
        # that should not occur but is cheap to guard).
        if [[ "${_RUNNER_SIGINT_RECEIVED:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.aborted" \
                "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                "reason=${_RUNNER_ABORT_REASON:-sigint}" "status=interrupted" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        # Fail-closed: if abort event cannot be emitted, that is still non-fatal for the trap
        # itself (the process is exiting), but we do not silently swallow the failure.
        if ! eb_emit_event "pipeline.abort" \
            "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" 2>/dev/null; then
            : # trap is exiting anyway; best-effort only
        fi
        # #525: terminal banner for the operator. Event already emitted above
        # so banner-render failure cannot lose the durable record. Reuses the
        # ✗ RED "aborted" rendering path (per ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
        # NB: do NOT redirect stderr away here — the banner writes to fd 2.
        # Wrap in a subshell so a non-zero rc inside doesn't abort the trap.
        ( _render_pipeline_end "aborted" ) || true
        # #2131: abnormal path — pipeline.aborted/pipeline.abort are on disk
        # now, so the sidecar's final render says why. Last, deliberately.
        _runner_status_comment_reap
    }
    # #612 / Wave 15-F (#686): INT/TERM trap — flag the signal cause then
    # exit. Setting the marker + reason before exit lets the EXIT trap emit
    # `pipeline.aborted reason=<sigint|sigterm>`; `exit 1` triggers
    # _runner_abort_trap (EXIT) which writes state + events. The signal is in
    # that reason, not in the exit status (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — it was 130/143).
    # ADR-025 (Wave 15-B #684): record the abort word in the cross-subshell
    # sentinel FIRST so any in-flight subshell (cycle iter, strategy fanout)
    # sees it via _zbuild_check_abort at its next boundary.
    _runner_signal_trap() {
        local _sig="${1:-INT}" _word="sigint"
        [[ "$_sig" == "TERM" ]] && _word="sigterm"
        _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "$_word"
        _RUNNER_SIGINT_RECEIVED=1
        # Wave 15-H (#688): flag-gated process-group signal forwarding. When
        # `set -m` is on (via ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1 at startup), every
        # child of this shell — backgrounded OR foreground subshell — has its
        # own PGID == its PID, so `kill -- -PID` reaches the whole subtree.
        # We enumerate direct children via two complementary sources:
        #   1. `jobs -p` — backgrounded jobs known to bash
        #   2. `pgrep -P $$` — all direct children, including foreground
        #      subshells bash does NOT list in `jobs -p`
        # We TERM each PGID, then schedule a 1s-grace KILL backstop for any
        # child that traps and ignores TERM. Per-site kills (Wave 8 build
        # plugin, Wave 15-G router) remain as fallback — this is belt-and-
        # suspenders, not replacement.
        #
        # Known limitation: bash defers signal-trap delivery until the
        # current foreground command returns. With `set -m`, a foreground
        # plugin subshell is in its own PGID, so a kernel-pgrp TERM to the
        # runner does NOT reach it directly; the trap fires only after the
        # subshell returns naturally. This is acceptable because:
        #   (a) the flag is OPT-IN (default OFF, byte-identical to today);
        #   (b) the router's Wave 15-G PG-kill already handles the slow
        #       claude-spawning path (the realistic blocker);
        #   (c) plugin dispatch now runs in the background (ADR-054 §7), so
        #       the trap runs at once and plugin_stop_running stops the stage.
        if [[ "${ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
            local _child_pid _pgid _pgids_snapshot="" _self_pgid=""
            # Resolve the runner's own PGID so we never signal it (would
            # be suicide; the trap's `exit` below handles runner teardown).
            if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                _self_pgid="$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
            fi
            _w15h_collect_pgid() {
                # Resolve a child PID to its current PGID via `ps` (which
                # is reliable even when the PID is not the group leader)
                # and append it to the dedup snapshot. Falls back to the
                # PID itself when `ps` cannot resolve (e.g. child already
                # exited) — kill is best-effort 2>/dev/null anyway.
                local _pid="$1" _resolved=""
                [[ -z "$_pid" ]] && return 0
                # #2131: the status-comment sidecar is reaped by the EXIT
                # trap AFTER pipeline.aborted is on disk — not swept here,
                # where the 1s KILL backstop would cut its final render.
                [[ "$_pid" == "${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}" ]] && return 0
                if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                    _resolved="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
                fi
                [[ -z "$_resolved" ]] && _resolved="$_pid"
                # Skip runner's own PGID — protects against self-signal
                # when a child's PGID resolved to the runner's group
                # (can happen when `set -m` was not effective for that
                # spawn site, e.g. a sync call that pre-dated the flag).
                [[ -n "$_self_pgid" && "$_resolved" == "$_self_pgid" ]] && return 0
                case " $_pgids_snapshot " in *" $_resolved "*) return 0;; esac
                _pgids_snapshot+="$_resolved "
            }
            # Source 1: bash-tracked background jobs.
            while IFS= read -r _child_pid; do
                _w15h_collect_pgid "$_child_pid"
            done < <(jobs -p 2>/dev/null)
            # Source 2: all direct children (catches foreground subshells
            # which bash does NOT list in `jobs -p`).
            if command -v pgrep >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                while IFS= read -r _child_pid; do
                    _w15h_collect_pgid "$_child_pid"
                done < <(pgrep -P $$ 2>/dev/null)
